ambient_events: A slot machine somewhere sings a jackpot no one won.
The cashier counts a strap of chips behind the bars without once looking up.
Somewhere a lever cranks down and three reels blur, then stop dead. A groan. Another credit gone.
A machine two rows over pays out in a clatter of coin, and every head in the room turns for a half-second of hope.
The neon over the door stutters, buzzes, and holds: a dying sign refusing to quit.
A woman in too much makeup works the slot row, laughing at jokes nobody's telling, watching for a wallet left open.
Two men have a low, ugly conversation by the cage. One of them isn't asking.
Security walks a sobbing man toward the back door with a hand on his neck. Nobody watches. Everybody watches.
Someone's been sick in the corner by the machines; a bored attendant throws sawdust on it and wanders off.
A cocktail waitress with dead eyes and a chrome tray threads the tables, comping drinks to whoever's losing fastest.
A hustler fans a deck for a stranger, all teeth and warmth, already counting the man's credits.
Someone whispers a number, a debt, a marker, a due date, and the air goes a half-degree colder.
The carpet gives a faint wet sound underfoot near the high table. Best not to look down.
A payphone by the restrooms rings, and rings, and stops. A moment later it starts again.
description: A low, windowless room drowned in dying neon and secondhand smoke, the carpet a violent paisley chosen decades ago to hide blood, ash, and worse, and doing all three at once. Felt tables ring a cashier's cage bolted down like it expects to be robbed, and every surface tilts a fraction toward the house. The air is climate-controlled to a permanent, luckless 2 a.m., and it smells of spilled liquor, ozone, and people losing money they didn't have to begin with. Behind the machines, a door with no handle leads somewhere nobody comes back from smiling. Under a low green-shaded lamp near the cage, an old woman deals a hand-shuffled game and calls every card aloud.

window.description: A full-height pane onto the street, kept just clean enough to trade through. Whatever the weather is doing out there, it is doing it in plain view.
window.name: the shopfront window

name: The Lucky Bastard
